answer: Agents buying pigment for a tundra research station use sealed bids to track the pulse of demand. Each bid commitment locks a deposit until its reveal deadline; failure to reveal forfeits it even if the account disappears. Every alias must fund its own deposit. A swarm cannot cheaply commit many bids and reveal only those profitable after prices move. Deposits must exceed the potential gain from selective non-revelation; this deters sybil option farming, not wealthy bidders.
